lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Something Went Wrong at the Bench
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Isabel Ladeia Tavares | Lesson 7 -- Something Went Wrong at the Bench
lesson.grammar_point: modal perfects: must have, might have, cannot have and should have

listenings.text: The worst mistake I made in my first year in a lab was not the mistake itself. It was the forty minutes afterwards. I had been asked to prepare a set of plates for somebody else's experiment, and when I checked them the next morning, every single one was cloudy. Contaminated. I knew straight away what must have happened. I must have left the lids off while I was labeling them, because I remembered being interrupted by a phone call halfway through. And for forty minutes I did the thing everybody does. I looked for a version of the story in which it was not me. The incubator might have been opened by somebody else. The batch of medium could have been bad. None of that was true, and I knew it. When I finally went to my supervisor, I said three sentences. The plates are contaminated. I think I must have left them open yesterday afternoon. I can have a new set ready by Thursday. She said thank you, and that was it. Nobody remembers the plates. What she remembered, and told me years later, was that I came to her first, before anybody else found out.

Morning, this is Paulo from the facilities team, and this is for whoever is responsible for the minus eighty freezer on the third floor. The alarm went off at around two in the morning, and the temperature had risen to minus forty by the time I got there. It cannot have been the power, because every other freezer on that corridor was fine, and the logs show no cut at all. My best guess is the door. Somebody must have opened it late yesterday, and the seal might have caught on the corner of a box, which happens more often than people think. I have closed it properly, it is back down to minus seventy-five, and it should be at full temperature again by lunchtime. Two things I need from you. First, check whether anything on the top two shelves should have been moved to the backup freezer, because those are the samples that warmed up the most. Second, and I am not looking for anybody to blame here, I need to know who used it last, so we can work out whether it was the door or the freezer itself. If it was the freezer, it has to be repaired this week.
